**Source of truth for database structure. Regenerated from live database queries.**

**Generated By:** REFRESH_SCHEMA.SQL export + automated processing
**Database:** Staging (InPersonMarketplace-Staging)

> ⚠️ **Structured tables (Columns / FKs / Indexes / Functions sections) are STALE as of 2026-04-24.** Migration 124 added 2 columns (`vendor_profiles.market_box_frequency`, `market_box_subscriptions.pickup_frequency`) and replaced 4 functions on Staging. The Change Log entry below documents what changed, but the structured-table sections still reflect pre-124 state. Run `supabase/REFRESH_SCHEMA.sql` on Staging and rebuild the structured tables when next convenient.

| 2026-08-02 | 20260802_216_ft_pickup_slot_capacity | **⏳ NOT YET APPLIED (written 2026-08-02; user applies Dev + Staging).** FT day-to-day pickup capacity + slot-time validation. **Problem:** nothing limited how many app orders a truck receives for the same pickup time — buyers DO pick a mandatory `preferred_pickup_time` (mig 028) but slots are generated client-side only and `time-slots.ts:26` says outright *"slots are waves, not reservations"*; nothing counted them, so 40 buyers could all pick 12:00, breaking the `_platform_skip_line` commitment. **5 new columns on `vendor_profiles`** (all nullable, **NULL = unlimited = today's behavior, INERT until a truck opts in**): `pickup_capacity_total_per_slot` (Q1, context only), **`pickup_capacity_app_orders` (ENFORCED order cap)**, `pickup_capacity_avg_items` (Q3), **`pickup_capacity_items` (ENFORCED item cap, = Q2×Q3, overridable)**, `pickup_capacity_slot_minutes` (15|30 — the slot length the caps were set against, so the UI can warn when a `pickup_lead_minutes` change makes them stale). **New partial index** `idx_order_items_pickup_slot (vendor_profile_id, market_id, pickup_date, preferred_pickup_time) WHERE preferred_pickup_time IS NOT NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL`. **2 new functions:** `check_pickup_slot_capacity(vendor, market, date, time, adding_items, order_id)` → advisory-locked (same shape as `book_weekly_booth_atomic` mig 186) count of DISTINCT orders + SUM(quantity) in that slot vs both caps, excluding cancelled items and cancelled/refunded orders so capacity frees on refund; returns allowed+reason+used/cap; service_role only. `validate_pickup_slot_time(vendor, market, date, time)` → closes the hole where "inside vendor hours / not past / past lead time" existed ONLY in client JS (server checked just a 15-min boundary, `cart/items:179-185`); all comparisons in the market's timezone (Vercel runs UTC); honors vendor per-market time overrides like mig 199/200. Slot length is **not fixed** — it's `pickup_lead_minutes` (15 or 30) per `time-slots.ts:49`. Events untouched (they use `event_waves`). Design + signed-off copy: `apps/web/.claude/backlog.md` top entry. `NOTIFY pgrst`. ROLLBACK in file. |
| 2026-08-01 | 20260801_215_tax_jurisdiction_reverify_on_address_change | **⏳ NOT YET APPLIED to any environment (written 2026-08-01; user applies Dev + Staging).** Guardrail for mig 214: nothing tied a market's stored tax jurisdictions to the address they were resolved from, so editing the address left them silently describing the OLD location while still stamped "verified" — confidently wrong tax data, invisible until an audit. **New trigger** `trg_clear_tax_jurisdiction_verification` (BEFORE UPDATE OF address, city, state, zip ON markets) → `clear_tax_jurisdiction_verification_on_address_change()`: nulls `tax_jurisdiction_verified_at` when any address component changes (`IS DISTINCT FROM`, so NULL↔value counts). **`tax_jurisdictions` itself is deliberately PRESERVED** — the admin re-verifies rather than re-entering; silently discarding their work would be its own failure. Trigger not route-validation so it catches EVERY write path (admin UI, `/api/markets` PATCH, manager edits, manual SQL). Mirrors mig 202's `clear_email_suppression_on_change`. Historical `order_items` rows unaffected (they snapshot their own rates — mig 214). Companion code: the tax-jurisdictions GET returns `needsReverification` (jurisdictions present + no stamp) and the admin card shows a loud amber "Re-verify needed" banner; PUT additionally rejects non-Texas markets and warns when a city-level jurisdiction name doesn't corroborate `markets.city`. No columns, no data change. `NOTIFY pgrst`. ROLLBACK in file. |
| 2026-08-01 | 20260801_214_tax_jurisdiction_storage | **Applied to Dev + Staging 2026-08-01 (user); Prod PENDING.** Sales-tax jurisdiction storage — step 1 of Texas readiness, deliberately built BEFORE any calculation. Rationale: as a marketplace provider we must file the long form (01-114) + **List Supplement (01-116)** — a per-jurisdiction table requiring the **seven-digit local code**, amount subject to tax, rate and tax due for every city/county/transit/SPD — **from the first return regardless of size** (Form 01-922 instr. Rev. 8-25); we are on **monthly** filing. Local rates change quarterly and refunds must reverse at the ORIGINAL rate, so unsnapshotted tax cannot be reconstructed; 4-year retention (§151.0242). **New columns — `markets` (5):** `tax_jurisdictions` (JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT `[]`, array of `{code,name,level(state|city|county|transit|spd),rate_pct}`), `tax_rate_total_pct` (NUMERIC(6,4)), `tax_rate_version` (TEXT, e.g. "2026-Q3"), `tax_jurisdiction_verified_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ), `tax_jurisdiction_note` (TEXT). **New CHECK** `ck_markets_tax_rate_ceiling` (rate NULL or 0–8.25, the TX statutory cap; added NOT VALID then VALIDATEd — instant, no existing non-NULL rows). **`order_items` (5):** `tax_amount_cents`, `taxable_amount_cents` (both CHECK ≥0), `tax_jurisdictions` (JSONB, frozen breakdown incl. per-jurisdiction `tax_cents`), `tax_rate_version`, `tax_source` (CHECK none|manual|stripe). Snapshot lives on ITEMS not orders because same-market is enforced only for `market_type='traditional'` (cart/validate:160) — private_pickup/event orders can span markets at different rates. **New partial index** `idx_order_items_tax_collected (created_at) WHERE tax_amount_cents IS NOT NULL AND > 0`. **`orders` (1):** `tax_total_cents` (CHECK ≥0) — reconciliation rollup only; item rows stay authoritative for filing. **NULL vs 0 is meaningful:** NULL = pre-tax-launch (no tax collected), 0 = computed and correctly zero (exempt item) — do not COALESCE away. Booth/vendor-space rentals intentionally get NO tax columns (space rental is not taxable in TX — Pub. 96-211). Subscriptions are out of scope (Stripe invoices, reported from Stripe Tax). Companion code (pure, no I/O, nothing wired to collection yet): `src/lib/tax/jurisdictions.ts` + 22 unit tests. ADDITIVE, no backfill, no behavior change. `NOTIFY pgrst`. ROLLBACK in file. Full context: `apps/web/.claude/sales_tax_readiness.md`. |

| 2026-05-20 | 20260520_144_booth_auto_assignment | **Applied to all 3 envs (Dev + Staging 2026-05-20, Prod 2026-06-02 Session 87).** Three changes in one migration, runs in a single transaction: (1) **New columns on `markets`:** `booth_label_start TEXT NULL`, `booth_label_end TEXT NULL` — optional manager-declared booth-label range (e.g., "1"/"8", "A1"/"A8", "Booth-1"/"Booth-8"). New error code: `LABELS_EXHAUSTED` (ERRCODE P0004) — raised when v_remaining > 0 but no label is available (manager's declared range is shorter than the inventory total). Existing error codes (OVERBOOKED P0001, DUPLICATE P0002, INVENTORY_NOT_FOUND P0003) unchanged. `SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public` preserved. Atomically replaces a market's opt-in selections: DELETE all existing selections for p_market_id, then INSERT new rows from p_selections JSONB array. Catalog validation (statement_ids must exist + be active) remains in the route layer; the function trusts pre-validated inputs. Returns rows with `selection_*` prefixed column names to avoid PL/pgSQL name shadowing on RETURNS TABLE columns. No schema changes (function-only migration). No structured-table regeneration needed. | 2026-05-18 | 20260518_142_book_weekly_booth_atomic | **Applied to all 3 envs (Dev + Staging 2026-05-18, Prod 2026-06-02 Session 87 — mig 149 re-run in same session per embedded reminder, then mig 152 stripped PUBLIC EXECUTE on this function too).** **New function:** `book_weekly_booth_atomic(p_vendor_profile_id UUID, p_market_id UUID, p_inventory_id UUID, p_week_start_date DATE, p_acceptance_id UUID) RETURNS TABLE(rental_id, rental_price_cents, rental_status, rental_week_start_date)` — `LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public`. ## Views

| View Name | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| active_markets | Markets with status=active and not expired |
| market_vendor_counts | Count of distinct vendors per market (published listings only) |
| v_error_frequency | Error report counts grouped by error_code |
| v_failed_approaches | Failed error_resolutions ordered by error_code |
| v_platform_admin_escalated_reports | Escalated error reports with joins to verticals, error_logs, error_resolutions |
| v_verified_solutions | Most recent verified error_resolution per error_code |
| v_vertical_admin_pending_reports | Pending/acknowledged vertical admin error reports |
| vendor_referral_summary | Vendor referral stats (pending/earned/applied counts and credits) |
| geography_columns | PostGIS system view |
| geometry_columns | PostGIS system view |
